name: pwa-install-card
description: R7-M / U2 (product audit 2026-09-25 §5 brief 3): the PWA install CTA + iOS coachmark. FOUR control arms, each with a failMessage naming what it protects against vacuous assertions: (1) the card must NOT appear before the getting-started checklist is complete; (2) it must NOT appear the instant the checklist completes but BEFORE its card is dismissed — the deliberate refinement that avoids colliding with the checklist's own still-visible 'Done' button in the same bottom-left slot; (3) it must NOT appear with the checklist done+dismissed but with no captured beforeinstallprompt — proving the event, not just the checklist, gates the CTA; (4) a showroom (viewOnly) visitor must never see it, and un-setting viewOnly must bring it straight back — proving live suppression, not a one-time boot check. Also drives the real Install-accept flow, a real 'Not now' click whose localStorage dismissal is verified to suppress a FRESH later beforeinstallprompt in the same browser (not just hide the current card), and the iOS coachmark (UA-gated, simulated via eval since no real device is available). A genuine full-document reload of this exact flow was attempted and dropped: it intermittently exceeded the harness's boot-splash-removal timeout under this session's concurrent load (unrelated to this feature — see docs/developer/pwa-install.md §8); the persistence claim itself is still covered here (a direct localStorage read right after the real click) and by PwaInstallCard.test.tsx's remount-based check.

steps.name: setup
steps.eval: (() => { try { localStorage.setItem('hdb_onboarded','1'); localStorage.removeItem('hdb_checklist'); localStorage.removeItem('hdb_install_dismissed'); localStorage.removeItem('hdb_ios_addtohome_dismissed') } catch {}; const s = window.__store.getState(); s.endTour?.(); s.setOnboardingOpen?.(false); s.dismissLocationPrompt?.(); s.setManualHour?.(13); s.setTimeMode?.('manual'); s.setWeather?.('clear'); s.setQualityTier?.('realistic'); s.setDeviceClass?.('capable'); s.hideLoading?.(); window.__store.setState({ checklistDone: [], checklistDismissed: false, viewOnly: false, cameraMode: 'orbit', floorPlanEditing: false, presenting: false }) })()

steps.name: pin-device-class
steps.eval: (() => { const s = window.__store; s.getState().setDeviceClass('capable'); s.setState({ setDeviceClass: () => {} }) })()

steps.name: control-1-no-card-before-checklist
steps.failMessage: CONTROL ARM BROKEN: the install card is showing before the getting-started checklist has even been touched — every assertion below about the checklist-complete trigger would prove nothing.

steps.name: control-2-no-card-while-checklist-still-shown
steps.failMessage: CONTROL ARM BROKEN: the install card appeared at the literal instant checklistDone hit 5/5, while the checklist's OWN 'Done' button card is still on screen in the SAME bottom-left slot. PwaInstallCard.tsx deliberately waits for checklistDismissed too, precisely to avoid this collision — see its doc comment.

steps.name: control-3-no-card-with-no-captured-event
steps.failMessage: CONTROL ARM BROKEN: the install card appeared with the checklist done+dismissed but NO beforeinstallprompt ever captured — the trigger must require BOTH the value moment AND a real deferred event, not the checklist alone.

steps.name: install-cta-shown
steps.failMessage: The install CTA did not appear after a simulated beforeinstallprompt at the value moment.

steps.name: installed-toast-shown
steps.failMessage: Clicking Install did not resolve through promptInstall() to an 'Installed' success toast.

steps.name: dismissal-persisted-to-localstorage
steps.eval: if (localStorage.getItem('hdb_install_dismissed') !== '1') throw new Error('Not now did not persist hdb_install_dismissed')

steps.name: card-stays-absent-after-dismissal
steps.failMessage: STICKY DISMISSAL REGRESSED: a FRESH beforeinstallprompt after the user explicitly clicked 'Not now' still re-offered the install CTA — the localStorage dismissal (just verified above) must suppress future offers in this browser, not just hide the one card that was on screen when it was clicked.

steps.name: set-ios-ua
steps.eval: Object.defineProperty(navigator, 'userAgent', { value: 'Mozilla/5.0 (iPhone; CPU iPhone OS 18_0 like Mac OS X) AppleWebKit/605.1.15 (KHTML, like Gecko) Version/18.0 Mobile/15E148 Safari/604.1', configurable: true })

steps.name: ios-coachmark-shown
steps.failMessage: The iOS coachmark did not appear on an iOS UA even though no beforeinstallprompt event exists there by construction (Safari has never implemented it).

steps.name: ios-dismissal-persisted
steps.eval: if (localStorage.getItem('hdb_ios_addtohome_dismissed') !== '1') throw new Error('Got it did not persist hdb_ios_addtohome_dismissed')

steps.name: ios-coachmark-stays-gone
steps.failMessage: STICKY DISMISSAL REGRESSED: the iOS coachmark reappeared on a later re-render in the SAME session after 'Got it' was clicked.

steps.name: restore-desktop-ua
steps.eval: Object.defineProperty(navigator, 'userAgent', { value: 'Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/120.0.0.0 Safari/537.36', configurable: true })

steps.name: control-4-card-visible-before-showroom
steps.failMessage: CONTROL ARM BROKEN: the install CTA is not showing in a NORMAL (non-showroom) session even after a fresh simulated event — the showroom-suppression assertions below would pass vacuously.

steps.name: flag-forced-off-in-showroom
steps.eval: if (window.__store.getState().featureFlags.pwaInstallPrompt !== false) throw new Error('pwaInstallPrompt flag was not forced off by viewOnly — it must be in VIEW_ONLY_BLOCKED_FLAGS')

steps.name: card-hidden-in-showroom
steps.failMessage: A showroom (viewOnly) visitor was offered installation — this is a deliberate product decision (installing the generic app shell does not carry the shared #/showroom/<code> design, since the manifest start_url is the app root, not the current URL fragment), not an oversight.

steps.name: card-reappears-after-leaving-showroom
steps.failMessage: The install CTA did not come back after leaving showroom mode — the suppression must be LIVE/reactive, not a one-time boot decision that then sticks incorrectly.
